tables.notes: Notes: Panel A uses standardized detailed CSRC industry codes. Observations without a valid standardized code are retained as a separate unknown-industry category only in these full-panel fixed-effect specifications. Baseline regressions and the original accounting specifications use firm-clustered standard errors. Financial controls comprise firm size, return on assets, leverage, and operating cash flow relative to assets. Full controls additionally include state ownership, listing age, and province effects. Panel E uses a fixed 47,731-observation sensitivity sample and changes only lagged opportunity intensity and diffusion by excluding each non-agricultural firm's own prior-calendar-year patent contribution. Relative to the common sample, this check excludes 42 non-agricultural firm-years in which the focal firm is the only non-agricultural firm in its lagged industry-year cell, leaving no benchmark after own-firm exclusion. Panel F retains point estimates and varies only the covariance estimator. Detailed-industry inference uses 73 clusters. The joint GTOS tests remain statistically significant, but industry-based clustering increases the standard errors of the agricultural coefficients. Panel G restricts the sample to 2013-2024, after the 2007-2012 window used to classify baseline high-intensity industries. It removes the early-window look-ahead feature without redefining the baseline high-intensity indicator. The diagnostics assess overlap, suppression, timing, and inference sensitivity. They do not rule out endogenous sorting, over-adjustment, collider-type conditioning, or omitted opportunity conditions. * p < 0.10, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01. An em dash in Panel F indicates that a joint GTOS-block test is not applicable to the control-adjusted model, which contains no GTOS variables.

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel H1. Gelbach components and firm-cluster bootstrap uncertainty

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel H2. Pooled-coefficient Oaxaca-style components and bootstrap uncertainty
tables.notes: Notes: Cells report point estimates (bootstrap SE) and 95% percentile intervals; shares and their SEs are percentages/percentage points. The baseline contains 47,773 firm-years from 4,290 firms. Each of 2,000 unstratified pairs-bootstrap draws samples 4,290 firms with replacement and retains each firm's complete common-sample history; repeated firms receive integer multiplicities. Firm-year N may vary across draws. The same draw is used for all outcomes and sparse, full, pooled, and auxiliary fits, with coefficients and group means recalculated. Seed 20261008 uses numpy default_rng/PCG64. Intervals are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles with linear interpolation; SEs use ddof=1. All 2,000 draws are estimable. Failed draws would be recorded without redraw or replacement. GTOS values, industry codes, and sample membership remain fixed; these intervals exclude proxy-construction, classification-source, and missing-support uncertainty and do not replace industry-based inference. Gelbach contributions sum to sparse minus full; Oaxaca gap = GTOS + other observed + remainder. Shares use the stated denominators, not the raw gap or explanatory power. No share denominator changes sign or falls below 1% of its original absolute point value in these draws; no ratios are trimmed. Wide offsetting individual components should not be interpreted as separate mechanisms. Values may not sum exactly because of rounding.

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel I. Fixed and jointly estimated NB2 dispersion
tables.notes: Notes: All models use the same 47,773 common-sample observations, 4,290 firm clusters, and 73 detailed-industry clusters. Sparse includes the agricultural indicator and year effects; control-adjusted adds six firm controls and province indicators; the next specification adds OI/OD; full adds FI. NB2 has a log link, no exposure offset or industry effects, and conditional variance mu + alpha times mu squared. The fixed alpha of 52.993677 is an unconditional moment heuristic, not a conditional dispersion MLE. Joint models estimate beta and log(alpha) by maximum likelihood. Cluster covariances use the complete score/Hessian including dispersion, with the finite-sample factor G/(G-1) times (N-1)/(N-K), where K includes alpha; intervals and significance use a normal reference. Exp(beta) is a conditional expected application-count ratio, not a probability, causal effect, or accounting share. Full-model firm-based ratio CI is [1.009, 1.804]; the industry interval includes one. All four retained BFGS fits satisfy convergence, finite-parameter, information-rank, and gradient checks. L-BFGS agrees for three; the control-adjusted L-BFGS fit fails a pre-set gradient criterion and is not substituted. Algebraically equivalent loggamma/log1p evaluation avoids underflow at tiny fitted means without deleting observations or changing NB2. * p < 0.10, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01.

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel J. Industry-cluster size and agricultural support
tables.notes: Notes: Cluster sizes count firm-years within each group in the fixed common sample. Agricultural observations occur in 38 of 73 industries; 35 contain none. Ten agricultural-support industries have fewer than ten agricultural firm-years. Group-specific top-five shares refer to the five largest industries for that group, not necessarily the same industries. There are 1,026 firms observed in more than one industry. Cluster counts and concentration describe support; they do not guarantee reliable industry-cluster inference. Component intervals in Panels H1-H2 use firm resampling and do not address industry dependence.

rows: Controls + own history + industry R&D + patent GTOS

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel K2. Own-patent-history diagnostic: industry-clustered inference
rows: Controls + own history + industry R&D + patent GTOS
tables.notes: Notes: All models use OLS with the agricultural indicator, six firm controls, and year and province indicators; no firm or industry fixed effects are added. Patent GTOS comprises the unchanged OI, OD, and FI variables. Model labels list additions to these controls. Panel K1 reports agricultural coefficients (firm-clustered SEs); Panel K2 reports the same coefficients (industry-clustered SEs) and industry-clustered 95% intervals. There are 4,219 firm and 64 industry clusters. Cluster covariances use G/(G-1) times (N-1)/(N-K), with K counting all fitted coefficients; intervals use a normal reference. In both history-plus-GTOS models, all three firm-based as well as industry-based intervals span zero. These intervals describe individual coefficients; they do not test coefficient changes between models. Prior patent counts do not capture all aspects of firm capability. Controlling for them may also absorb associations with the industry environment. The diagnostic does not identify independent opportunity, eliminate sorting, or quantify overlap removed. The selected auxiliary sample does not replace the main common sample. No empirical randomization or new seed is involved; software versions are the same as for the R&D regressions in Table A9.

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel L. Leave-one-industry-out accounting sensitivity
tables.notes: Notes: Coefficient change is full minus control-adjusted agricultural coefficient. Sparse includes the agricultural indicator and year indicators; control-adjusted adds the six firm controls and province indicators; full adds OI, OD, and FI. The Gelbach GTOS component sums OI, OD, and FI contributions to the sparse-minus-full coefficient difference; its share uses that difference as the denominator. Ranges are minima and maxima across all 73 deletions, not confidence intervals. The control-adjusted coefficient is negative and the full coefficient positive in every deletion for all three outcomes. This is a single-industry influence diagnostic, not a correction for sample selection or absent industry support. Positive full coefficients do not imply an agricultural advantage. Rounding may affect displayed values.

tables.caption: Table A2. Baseline patent regressions and model diagnostics
tables.panel: Panel M. Shared-industry accounting sensitivity
tables.notes: Notes: Sparse includes the agricultural indicator and year indicators; control-adjusted adds six firm controls and province indicators; full adds OI, OD, and FI. Coefficient change is full minus control-adjusted agricultural coefficient. The joint Gelbach GTOS component sums OI, OD, and FI contributions to the sparse-minus-full coefficient difference; its share uses that difference, not the control-minus-full difference. All three absolute GTOS components decrease after restriction; the shares increase because their denominators also decrease. The retained sample has 444 jointly populated, 16 agricultural-only and 162 non-agricultural-only industry-year cells, so it does not establish industry-year or multivariate common support. This comparison retains between-industry variation; it is not an industry-fixed-effect analysis or a missing-sample correction. Values are point estimates without new standard errors or confidence intervals; positive full coefficients do not imply an agricultural advantage. Rounding may affect displayed values.

tables.notes: Notes: Panel D covers every exclusion from the full panel. Panels E-F instead compare the common sample with the 838 post-2007, static-control-complete observations lacking at least one GTOS variable: 77 agricultural and 761 non-agricultural rows. tables.notes: Notes: The primary GTOS patent-activity grouping uses all 47,773 common-sample observations. The high-activity group contains 801 agricultural firm-years from 100 firms across 24 industries. Industry-year cells are ranked by an equal-weight mean of standardized lagged opportunity intensity and diffusion, split into pooled tertiles, and baseline high-intensity industries are assigned to the high-activity group. Bootstrap intervals use 2,000 firm-cluster replications and preserve firm-year weighting within sampled firms. Upper-tail-capped estimates are one-sided tail diagnostics, not winsorized estimates. Alternative definitions generally preserve a negative raw mean gap in the high-activity group, but upper-tail capping shows that its magnitude remains sensitive to extreme patent counts. Panel E restricts both firm groups to industries with at least the stated number of agricultural observations in the high-activity group. It therefore excludes non-agricultural observations from industries with no agricultural observations in that group. These comparisons are descriptive. The negative raw mean gap is not evidence of stable agricultural underperformance: the agricultural median exceeds the non-agricultural median, and p95 capping changes the mean gap to +0.098. The central conclusion concerns lower representation, not lower outcomes within this group.

tables.notes: Notes: The R&D environment is a general innovation-input benchmark and is not green-specific. Its monetary measure is lagged ln(1 + disclosed R&D in CNY per non-agricultural firm). The green-investment source is a 1999-2024 disclosure dataset compiled from listed-company annual reports, with the relevant firm scope identified using the Ministry of Ecology and Environment of China's industry-classification list for environmental verification of listed companies. Its measure is the lagged industry-year mean of ln(1 + capitalized green investment) among at least three non-agricultural disclosers; non-disclosure is missing rather than zero. Monetary amounts are used as reported and are not price-deflated. Time-adjusted estimates use equal-weight industry-year regressions with year effects and detailed-industry-clustered standard errors; within-year rank correlations use annual percentile ranks. Supported time-adjusted cells span 2008-2024 for R&D and 2009-2024 for green investment. These checks reduce common annual-trend concerns but do not resolve industry sorting. The comparisons provide convergent measurement evidence only and do not establish exogenous technological opportunity or causal validity.

tables.notes: Notes: Panels B-D are additional regression comparisons, distinct from Panel A's monetary R&D correlations and coverage. Regular consolidated reports dated 31 December supply R&D-to-revenue percentages and R&D personnel shares. The benchmark uses firms from the full panel that are not included in the CCAD agricultural list and have valid same-year detailed codes, not only control-complete firms. The mean is the unweighted average of firm-level disclosed ratios in percentage points, not a ratio of industry totals. At least three valid disclosers are required per industry-year. The median sensitivity uses the same records and support. Source year s is matched to outcome year s+1 without carrying values across gaps; public release dates are not verified. Non-disclosure and unsupported cells remain missing; disclosed zero is retained. One negative R&D/revenue ratio is ineligible and not recoded to zero; ratios above 100% remain valid, without caps. Personnel shares must lie in [0,100]. All models include six firm controls and province/year indicators, but no industry effects. Patent GTOS includes OI/OD/FI; non-patent models replace all three with R&D intensity, or with R&D intensity plus personnel share. Each set holds its sample fixed. Primary N=42,261 (4,221 firms; 64 industry clusters); personnel N=30,658 (4,175 firms; 63 industry clusters), restricted to 2016-2024 because regular personnel disclosure expands from 2015. Differences between these sets cannot be attributed only to personnel controls. Retention from the original common sample is 78.6% for agricultural and 89.3% for non-agricultural observations in the primary comparison. Observations excluded from the R&D-matched sample are less patent-active than retained observations (Panel B). The disclosure requirement therefore introduces additional sample selection. Standard errors use firm or industry clustering with finite-sample correction and normal-reference inference. Coefficient movements are point comparisons, not tests of their differences. General R&D is not green-specific or exogenous; these comparisons do not independently replicate the patent-based reversal. Panels B-D contain R&D regressions, distinct from the CSMAR environmental-ratio comparisons in Panels E-F; no price-deflation analysis is claimed. * p < 0.10, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01.

tables.panel: Panel H2. Agricultural coefficients in fixed-sample official-guide comparisons
tables.notes: Notes: Cells report agricultural coefficients, followed by (firm-clustered SE; detailed-industry-clustered SE). Count is green invention applications, log count is ln(1 + count) including zeros, and entry is the positive-count indicator. The Controls model includes the original six firm controls, intercept, and year/province indicators. Patent GTOS adds lagged OI, OD, and FI. The Guide profiles model instead adds all complete nominal profiles, without patent GTOS. Count/log count use OLS; entry uses LPM; no firm or industry fixed effects are added. Within each role-specific sample, all models and outcomes use the same observations. Cluster covariances use G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-K). The last two columns use industry t(G-1), with 19/12 degrees of freedom; firm inference uses the normal reference. Intervals condition on constructed classifications and do not cover coding uncertainty. Changes are point comparisons, not paired tests. Static profiles add no separately identifiable variation beyond detailed industry indicators; 20/13 industry clusters and selected domains limit inference. Positive coefficients do not establish an agricultural advantage or independent opportunity validation.
